sections.title: Primary data
sections.description: The publisher-deposited complete Ec_Syn57 design; no measured isolate or assay layer is attached.

items.citation: Nyerges A et al. Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution. Nature Communications (2026). doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9.
items.contribution: Publisher Source Data file Ec_Syn57.gb supplies the complete 3,973,902 bp circular design, its native coordinates and annotation. File SHA-256 8c61aeebfb8fef71a9d01ceba2a2acdb8babdf96ac0aa01aae36b10d08f77f96; sequence SHA-256 5ad86e64fa142b009c159dddd4c1eccf5cce6e8bafa8c374cbfb6e9bc8e07033. The article describes a complete E. coli genome and distinguishes it from a strain with a distinct recoding scheme. This is a design record, not a sequenced isolate; no omics, growth, fitness or partial-isolate measurement is assigned to it. The article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; this derived viewer payload follows the owner's citation-only admission decision of 2026-10-06.

sections.title: Methods and tools
sections.description: Sequence-derived calculations applied to the design, not measurements.

items.citation: Sharp PM, Li WH. The codon adaptation index—a measure of directional synonymous codon usage bias, and its potential applications. Nucleic Acids Research 15, 1281–1295 (1987). doi:10.1093/nar/15.3.1281.
items.contribution: Defines CAI. The design uses its own 84-gene translation-machinery reference set, a sequence-derived convention rather than measured expression.

items.citation: dos Reis M, Savva R, Wernisch L. Solving the riddle of codon usage preferences: a test for translational selection. Nucleic Acids Research 32, 5036–5044 (2004). doi:10.1093/nar/gkh834.
items.contribution: Defines the tRNA adaptation index and wobble/zero-weight conventions. This design uses the explicitly qualified approximate source-note annotation model, not established genomic anticodons, charging or expression measurements.

items.citation: Soma A et al. An RNA-modifying enzyme that governs both the codon and amino acid specificities of isoleucine tRNA. Molecular Cell 12, 689–698 (2003). doi:10.1016/S1097-2765(03)00346-0.
items.contribution: Supports the bacterial lysidine/TilS convention for Ile-CAT decoding ATA. The design model applies this convention to interpreted source notes; it is not a direct modification or charging measurement.

items.citation: Wright F. The ‘effective number of codons’ used in a gene. Gene 87, 23–29 (1990). doi:10.1016/0378-1119(90)90491-9.
items.contribution: Defines ENC and its GC3-based expected curve. Short-family substitutions remain labelled implementation conventions.

items.citation: Coleman JR et al. Virus attenuation by genome-scale changes in codon pair bias. Science 320, 1784–1787 (2008). doi:10.1126/science.1155761.
items.contribution: Motivates the codon-pair log-odds feature. Scores are fitted to the design sequence; no viral measurements or attenuation outcomes are transferred.

items.citation: McInnes L, Healy J, Saul N, Großberger L. UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection. Journal of Open Source Software 3, 861 (2018). doi:10.21105/joss.00861; umap-learn software.
items.contribution: umap-learn computes the design risk-feature embedding. Proximity is a visualization of calculated features, not evidence of shared function.

items.citation: Pedregosa F et al. Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python. Journal of Machine Learning Research 12, 2825–2830 (2011).
items.contribution: StandardScaler and PCA fit the design native codon coordinates. No parent-fixed projection or empirical phenotype is inferred.

items.citation: Lorenz R et al. ViennaRNA Package 2.0. Algorithms for Molecular Biology 6, 26 (2011). doi:10.1186/1748-7188-6-26; ViennaRNA 2.7.2.
items.contribution: ViennaRNA computes minimum-free-energy folds for design RNA windows and recoded simulations. The browser ships the locally compiled 2.7.2 engine. Credit to the ViennaRNA authors and the Institute for Theoretical Chemistry, University of Vienna; its license and build record are retained at site/vendor/viennarna/PROVENANCE.md.

items.citation: Emscripten 4.0.15 and bundled runtime components: musl, LLVM compiler-rt, Joseph A. Adams’s JSON library, and Doug Lea’s dlmalloc; upstream licenses retained with the ViennaRNA browser build.
items.contribution: Emscripten compiled the ViennaRNA engine to WebAssembly and supplied its JavaScript/runtime glue. The component-specific notices and licenses are retained under site/vendor/viennarna/; this is software attribution, not a source of biological data.

items.citation: Cock PJA et al. Biopython: freely available Python tools for computational molecular biology and bioinformatics. Bioinformatics 25, 1422–1423 (2009). doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp163.
items.contribution: The data-build and consistency checks use Biopython to parse biological sequence records, translate CDSs, and apply codon tables. No Biopython code is bundled with the site.

items.citation: NCBI. The Genetic Codes: The Bacterial, Archaeal and Plant Plastid Code (translation table 11).
items.contribution: Defines bacterial codon assignments and initiation semantics for local design translations and synonymous simulations. Local derived-protein identifiers are not NCBI accessions.

items.citation: Harris CR et al. Array programming with NumPy. Nature 585, 357–362 (2020). doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2.
items.contribution: NumPy arrays support the feature build and independent consistency checks; this package provides computation, not external gene measurements.

sections.title: Inherited functional annotations
sections.description: Admitted reference annotations transferred through unique full-length identical proteins. No recoded measurement, lab review, category inference or exact experimental parent claim.

items.citation: NCBI RefSeq. Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 assembly GCF_000005845.2 (ASM584v2), chromosome NC_000913.3; record release 2 September 2026; retrieved 5 October 2026.
items.contribution: Source of the chromosome sequence, CDS records, locus tags, gene symbols and products, coordinates, translation exceptions, and tRNA annotations used by this dataset. The pinned GenBank COMMENT states that annotation updates are derived from EcoCyc and that the update was generated by a collaboration including EcoCyc, the University of Wisconsin, UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot, and NCBI, so this release attributes its annotation to both NCBI RefSeq and EcoCyc (ledger decision 2026-10-06). The build used the genomic FASTA and GFF, CDS and protein FASTA files, assembly report, GenBank record, and NCBI checksum manifest.

items.citation: Keseler IM, Gama-Castro S, Mackie A, et al. The EcoCyc Database in 2021. Frontiers in Microbiology 12, 711077 (2021). doi:10.3389/fmicb.2021.711077. EcoCyc, SRI International, https://ecocyc.org; BioCyc, https://biocyc.org.
items.contribution: The curated source of the gene names, products, and gene-model updates that NCBI RefSeq carries for this genome: every GFF gene bears an ECOCYC cross-reference and the record names EcoCyc as the origin of its annotation updates. No EcoCyc file was downloaded or redistributed; this dataset is derived from the RefSeq record. Includes BioCyc™ pathway/genome databases under license from SRI International, which permits use and redistribution of the EcoCyc open database with attribution, a link to www.biocyc.org, and notification to SRI (owner action, 2026-10-06).

items.citation: Blattner FR, Plunkett G 3rd, Bloch CA, et al. The complete genome sequence of Escherichia coli K-12. Science 277, 1453–1462 (1997). doi:10.1126/science.277.5331.1453. GenBank U00096.3.
items.contribution: The original K-12 MG1655 genome sequence, maintained since as GenBank U00096 and mirrored by RefSeq NC_000913.3, from which every coordinate, codon, and folding window in this dataset is taken.

items.citation: The UniProt Consortium. UniProt: the Universal Protein Knowledgebase in 2025. Nucleic Acids Research 53, D609–D617 (2025). doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1010. UniProtKB proteome UP000000625 (Escherichia coli K-12), TSV retrieved 2026-10-06.
items.contribution: The curated function text, protein name, existence level and entry identity shown for each E. coli gene under "Annotation evidence", joined to the RefSeq locus tag through the entry's ordered locus name (b number) by tools/ecoli_annotation_layer.py; 4,403 reviewed entries, 4,384 loci joined, 3,118 with a function statement. An entry naming several loci is carried to each with its ambiguity stated. UniProtKB data are CC BY 4.0.

items.citation: Gene Ontology Consortium. UniProt-GOA proteome annotation file 18.E_coli_MG1655.goa (generated 2026-07-28, GO version 2026-07-26); Ashburner M et al., Nature Genetics 25, 25–29 (2000), doi:10.1038/75556; Gene Ontology Consortium, The Gene Ontology knowledgebase in 2026, Nucleic Acids Research (2025), doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1292; term names from go-basic.obo release 2026-05-19.
items.contribution: Evidence-coded Gene Ontology relationships in gene details and GO-term search for E. coli: every row of the GOA file joined to a locus through its UniProtKB accession (54,062 relationships over 3,900 site genes, assigned by EcoCyc, UniProt, InterPro, GO_Central and others; evidence codes kept, computational and experimental alike).
